slot.brief: Combustion of an organic compound containing C, H and O: from masses of CO2 and H2O collected, deduce percentage of oxygen and then the molecular formula using an independent molar-mass clue.

stem: A $0.90$ g sample of a compound containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen gives $1.32$ g of $\text{CO}_2$ and $0.54$ g of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ on complete combustion. If its molar mass is $90$ g mol$^{-1}$, find its molecular formula. Use $\text{C}=12$, $\text{H}=1$ and $\text{O}=16$.

verdicts.working: n(C) = 1.32/44 = 0.03 mol; n(H) = 2(0.54/18) = 0.06 mol. Oxygen mass = 0.90 − 0.36 − 0.06 = 0.48 g, so n(O) = 0.03 mol. The atom ratio is 1:2:1, giving empirical formula CH₂O (30 g mol⁻¹). The molar mass is 3 times this, so the molecular formula is C₃H₆O₃.

working:
$n_{\text{C}}=\dfrac{1.32}{44}=0.030\,\text{mol};\quad n_{\text{H}}=2\left(\dfrac{0.54}{18}\right)=0.060\,\text{mol}$
$m_{\text{O}}=0.90-(0.030\times12)-(0.060\times1)=0.48\,\text{g};\quad n_{\text{O}}=\dfrac{0.48}{16}=0.030\,\text{mol}$
$\text{C:H:O}=1:2:1\Rightarrow\text{empirical formula} = \text{CH}_2\text{O}$
$\dfrac{90}{30}=3\Rightarrow\text{molecular formula} = \text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$

Independent check: n(C) = 1.32/44 = 0.03 mol; n(H) = 2(0.54/18) = 0.06 mol. Oxygen mass = 0.90 − 0.36 − 0.06 = 0.48 g, so n(O) = 0.03 mol. The atom ratio is 1:2:1, giving empirical formula CH₂O (30 g mol⁻¹). The molar mass is 3 times this, so the molecular formula is C₃H₆O₃.
solution:
From the combustion products, $n_C=1.32/44=0.030$ mol and $n_H=2(0.54/18)=0.060$ mol. The oxygen mass is $0.90-(0.030)(12)-(0.060)(1)=0.48$ g, so $n_O=0.48/16=0.030$ mol.
Thus the atom ratio is $C:H:O=1:2:1$, giving empirical formula $CH_2O$ with molar mass $30$ g mol$^{-1}$. Since $90/30=3$, the molecular formula is $C_3H_6O_3$. (C)
